values.doc: INVALID_ARGUMENT: the request has a field the schema does not know.
INVALID_ARGUMENT: a page token was reused with different parameters.
INVALID_ARGUMENT / 422: an Idempotency-Key was reused with another body.
ABORTED: the first call with this Idempotency-Key is still running.
ABORTED: the etag sent does not match the Resource's current etag.
NOT_FOUND: the named Resource does not exist or is not visible.
ALREADY_EXISTS: a Resource with this name exists.
UNAUTHENTICATED: no valid key or token was presented.
PERMISSION_DENIED: the key lacks the method's permission.
FAILED_PRECONDITION: the controller reported Stalled or Ready=FALSE.
FAILED_PRECONDITION / 402: the plan's limit is reached.
FAILED_PRECONDITION / 402: the org's spend limit is reached.
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: the rate limit is reached; see Retry-After.
FAILED_PRECONDITION: the Resource is in a state that forbids the call.
INTERNAL: an internal fault; the cause is in Observability by request id.

UNAVAILABLE: the Resource store, the owning service's backend, or the
key verifier's snapshot is unavailable; retry after Retry-After.
UNIMPLEMENTED: the path or method is not served (yet) at this version.

UNAUTHENTICATED / 401: a key created seconds ago has not reached the
cell serving this request yet; retry within `active_after_ms`.
DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: the client deadline passed before the work committed.
NOT_FOUND: no method is served at this path.

UNAVAILABLE: the backend serves another contract image than the API
endpoint for this service; the Release rolls them in order.

UNAVAILABLE / 503: no machine can be granted now (immediate-or-fail);
retry after Retry-After.
FAILED_PRECONDITION / 422: the requested shape or kind is not sold.

ABORTED / 409: the call named a lease generation or control epoch that is
no longer current.

FAILED_PRECONDITION / 409: the Resource is attached to or held by another
Resource, for example a volume attached to a running lease.

FAILED_PRECONDITION / 409: another holder has input control of the
display.

FAILED_PRECONDITION / 409: a human has taken over the display; agent input
and screenshots are refused until control is released or expires.

INVALID_ARGUMENT: a name segment is not a current id, and no id map row
moves it (identifiers-convergence.md §4.4).

INVALID_ARGUMENT: the `If-Match` header and the request's `etag` name
different etags; send one, or the same.

INVALID_ARGUMENT: the method has no dry run; a request with
`validate_only` is refused before anything is written.

308 on GET/HEAD: the id in the name moved in the identifiers cut;
`Location` and `Sylphx-Moved-To` carry the new one, and the body is
`{"error":"id_moved","old":…,"new":…}`, for the 14-day window of the
owning service (identifiers-convergence.md §4.4). The Resource-API
moved-id resolver answers it in front of every service.

error_codes.doc: INVALID_ARGUMENT: the request has a field the schema does not know.
INVALID_ARGUMENT: a field failed validation.
INVALID_ARGUMENT: a page token was reused with different parameters.
INVALID_ARGUMENT / 422: an Idempotency-Key was reused with another body.
ABORTED: the first call with this Idempotency-Key is still running.
ABORTED: the etag sent does not match the Resource's current etag.
NOT_FOUND: the named Resource does not exist or is not visible.
ALREADY_EXISTS: a Resource with this name exists.
UNAUTHENTICATED: no valid key or token was presented.
PERMISSION_DENIED: the key lacks the method's permission.
FAILED_PRECONDITION: `spec.deletion_protection` blocks the delete.
FAILED_PRECONDITION: the controller reported Stalled or Ready=FALSE.
FAILED_PRECONDITION / 402: the plan's limit is reached.
FAILED_PRECONDITION / 402: the org's spend limit is reached.
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: the rate limit is reached; see Retry-After.
FAILED_PRECONDITION: the Resource is in a state that forbids the call.
INTERNAL: an internal fault; the cause is in Observability by request id.

UNAVAILABLE: the Resource store, the owning service's backend, or the
key verifier's snapshot is unavailable; retry after Retry-After.
UNIMPLEMENTED: the path or method is not served (yet) at this version.

UNAUTHENTICATED / 401: a key created seconds ago has not reached the
cell serving this request yet; retry within `active_after_ms`.
DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: the client deadline passed before the work committed.
NOT_FOUND: no method is served at this path.

UNAVAILABLE: the backend serves another contract image than the API
endpoint for this service; the Release rolls them in order.

UNAVAILABLE / 503: no machine can be granted now (immediate-or-fail);
retry after Retry-After.
FAILED_PRECONDITION / 422: the requested shape or kind is not sold.

ABORTED / 409: the call named a lease generation or control epoch that is
no longer current.

FAILED_PRECONDITION / 409: the Resource is attached to or held by another
Resource, for example a volume attached to a running lease.

FAILED_PRECONDITION / 409: another holder has input control of the
display.

FAILED_PRECONDITION / 409: a human has taken over the display; agent input
and screenshots are refused until control is released or expires.

INVALID_ARGUMENT: a name segment is not a current id, and no id map row
moves it (identifiers-convergence.md §4.4).

INVALID_ARGUMENT: the `If-Match` header and the request's `etag` name
different etags; send one, or the same.

INVALID_ARGUMENT: the method has no dry run; a request with
`validate_only` is refused before anything is written.

308 on GET/HEAD: the id in the name moved in the identifiers cut;
`Location` and `Sylphx-Moved-To` carry the new one, and the body is
`{"error":"id_moved","old":…,"new":…}`, for the 14-day window of the
owning service (identifiers-convergence.md §4.4). The Resource-API
moved-id resolver answers it in front of every service.

messages.doc:
TargetingCondition compares one attribute of the evaluation context with a
value. The public contract is structured rather than an expression
language (CEL): every SDK evaluates rules locally, and a small table of
operators is the same in Rust, TypeScript and any later SDK without an
expression runtime in each; a write is checked field by field against the
schema; a console and an agent edit fields, not source text; and
evaluation cost is bounded by the rule's size, with no program to run.
The operators are the ones customers already used.

fields.doc:
`user_id`, `anonymous_id`, or a path into the context's `attributes`,
dot-separated (`plan`, `device.os`). Required, except with IN_SEGMENT and
NOT_IN_SEGMENT.

messages.doc:
TargetingRule serves a value to evaluations that match its conditions, to
a stable percentage of them.

Percentages use one bucket per flag and evaluation subject: bucket =
FNV-1a 32-bit of the UTF-8 string `{config_flag}:{subject}`, mod 100,
where `{config_flag}` is the flag's id and `{subject}` the value of
`bucket_attribute`. A rule matches when bucket < percentage. The bucket
does not depend on the rule, so rules on the same attribute split
cumulatively: 30/30/40 across three values is three rules at 30, 60 and
100, and a subject keeps its bucket when the percentage grows.

fields.doc: The value served when the rule matches; of the flag's type.
fields.name: value

fields.doc:
Serve `value` to evaluations whose bucket is below this, from 0 to 100;
default 100. The rest fall through to the next rule.
fields.name: percentage

fields.doc:
The context attribute hashed for the bucket: `user_id`, `anonymous_id`,
or an attribute path; default `user_id`, else `anonymous_id`. An
evaluation without it never matches a rule below 100 percent.
fields.name: bucket_attribute

fields.doc: What the rule is for.
fields.name: description

fields.doc:
Conditions over the evaluation context; all must hold. None matches
every evaluation.

messages.doc:

mints with its own server key for one end user, who approves the
provider's consent there. The mailbox it connects lives in the customer's
environment, and the end user signs in to nothing of Sylphx and sees no
Sylphx name. It is single use and expires (the Stripe Account Link model):
pressing Continue on the page claims it, so a link preview's fetch does
not; a claimed or expired link sends the end user to `refresh_url`, where
the customer's server mints a new one.

(run-distributed-jobs.md §4). A run splits its work into shards that

authenticated this request. Clients fill their org, project, and env
defaults from it; every valid key may call it, whatever its scopes.

methods.doc: Captures an existing grant for one session and purpose; never issues a key.
Rotates the captured value under the same handle with generation fencing.
Revokes one captured handle. Repeating the revocation is harmless.
Creates an agent and its version 1.

Updates an agent. A change to `spec` mints the next AgentVersion;
sessions already started keep the version they pinned.

Deletes an agent and its versions. An agent with sessions is refused
with `INVALID_STATE` unless `force` is set, which deletes them too.
Atomically admits a pinned task session, initial event and pending turn.
Lists an agent's versions, newest first.

Guest execution capability authentication, not an Access management key.
Preserve any JSON tool result, including scalars and arrays.
The immutable pinned HTTP-tool catalog exposed to the guest's MCP bridge.

Starts a session of an agent, pinned to its current version unless
`agent_version` names another. Requires a secret key until end-user
ownership is implemented. The session starts idle; `:send` starts its
first turn.

Lists sessions, newest first. With a publishable key, only the caller's
end user's sessions.

Deletes a session and its events. A session whose turn is running is
refused with `INVALID_STATE` unless `force` is set, which interrupts it
first.

Sends a message into the running turn; the agent reads it at its next
step. On an idle session it is the same as `:send`.

Stops the running turn at its current step. Calls already made keep
their results; the session becomes idle. A no-op on an idle session.
Answers a tool call waiting for approval; the turn continues.
Returns the result of a client tool call; the turn continues.

Lists a session's events in sequence order. To follow a session, call
again with the filter `sequence > N`, N the last sequence read; `wait`
holds the call open until a newer event is appended or the wait ends.

Deletes a memory store. A store an agent names is refused with
`RESOURCE_IN_USE`; a store with memories is refused with `INVALID_STATE`
unless `force` is set, which deletes them too.

Lists a store's memories, newest first. With a publishable key, only the
caller's end user's memories.
Deletes a memory. An end user may delete their own.

Recalls the memories that best match a query, by hybrid full-text and
vector search. With a publishable key, only the caller's end user's
memories. A read with a request body, like a query.

services.doc:
AgentsService is Sylphx Agents, the platform's hosted agent runtime
(ADR-01M495TCCBZGSQ68A4P4G428H2). Apps call it instead of building their
own agent loop, session store, memory and credential handling.

Scopes: `agents:read` and `agents:write` manage agents, versions and
memory stores with a secret key. `agents:sessions` runs sessions and reads
and deletes session and memory records. All methods currently require a
secret key. Publishable-key access is deferred until the backend enforces
end-user ownership of sessions and memories and `end_user_access` on Agents.
Credential actions capture existing grants; handles are not CRUD resources.
services.name: agents

methods.doc: Lists the admitted catalog; filter by `brand`, `modality`, or `model`.

services.doc:
AiService is the Resource side of Sylphx AI: the model catalog.

Inference is not here. The OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible routes
(`/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/embeddings`,
`/v1/images/*`, `/v1/audio/*`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/files`) keep their
industry wire and stay outside the Resource grammar (ai-inference-surface.md
§4, resource-api-and-clients.md §4.6); their contract is imported OpenAPI,
not proto. Usage is not here either: AI keeps no usage or spend table
(AI-USAGE-SPEND); its meters are read from Kernel Billing.
services.name: ai

methods.doc: Lists a project's artifacts; filter by `digest`, `kind`, or `subject`.
Registers an artifact whose bytes were pushed by digest; verification runs after.
Deletes an artifact; fails while a Release references it or a legal hold is active.

services.doc:
ArtifactsService is Sylphx Artifacts: immutable content by digest, with
its SBOM and provenance. Sylphx Build writes them; Release reads them.
services.name: artifacts

methods.doc:
Lists assets. The filter is limited to `kind`, `state`, and
`review_state`.

Exports every servable variant in the environment as one flat, paged
manifest, independent of the keys the code declares. Rejected and retired
variants are left out unless `filter` asks for their `review_state`. The
last page carries a digest a client checks to know it holds the whole set.

Records the recipes as assets and generates the variants that are
missing. Each call is idempotent and works within a bounded time; call
again until `pending` is 0.

Returns the `assets.lock` entries and canonical text for the keys the call
names, and only those. A read with a request body, like a query.
Approves one variant and records who approved it.

Rejects one variant. Its slot is freed and the next `:generate` fills it;
the rejected file keeps serving at its URL.

Retires one variant. Its URL answers 404 from then on and its slot is
freed.

services.doc:
AssetsService is Sylphx Generated Assets: declare images in code, generate
them once, lock them, and serve them from a CDN by content hash. An Asset
holds a recipe and its variants; `:generate` makes what is missing, and
`:lock` returns the `assets.lock` text a build commits. Generation happens
only in these calls, never at build or run time.
services.name: assets

methods.doc: Suspends an end user: sessions are revoked and sign-in is refused.
Clears an end user's sign-in lock (repeated failed sign-ins) now.
Revokes every session of an end user.

Sets the customer's own id for an end user, once: an unset namespace is
written, a set one is never rewritten, and a different value for a set
namespace is refused. A namespace holds one id for the life of the user.
Erasure removes the ids and remembers their hashes, so a value that
belonged to an erased user is never handed to another one.

Finds the one end user of one of the customer's own ids. An id that
belongs to no live user of this environment is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`,
the same answer a value erased with its user gives.
Gets an identity of an end user.
Lists the identities an end user signs in with.

Moves a federated or device identity from one end user to another, to
fix a wrongly linked player. One transaction: the identity changes owner,
the sessions of both end users are revoked, and nothing else about
either moves (profile, memberships, data). Refused when it would leave
the source with no sign-in, unless the source is suspended, and when the
target already has an identity of the same provider. The reason is
audited with the operator, both end users and the identity's fingerprint.
An operator action: an end user's own session cannot call it.

Accepts a pending invitation for an end user whose verified email is the
invited address, and creates the membership.
Creates an email domain; the answer names the TXT record to publish.
Looks up the domain's TXT record now; found, the domain is verified.

Issues a new client secret, returned once; the old one verifies until
`grace_period` ends.

services.doc:
AuthService is Sylphx Auth's management surface: sign-in for a customer's
own users, their sessions, customer organizations, and OAuth clients.
Sylphx orgs, members, principals, and keys are Sylphx Access, never Auth.
End-user ceremonies (sign-in, recovery, OAuth authorize and token) are
protocol endpoints, not Resource methods.
services.name: auth

methods.doc: Lists meters. Anonymous-readable: the pricing page renders from it.
Lists the plans the caller can see. Anonymous-readable: the pricing page renders from it.
Lists an org's billing accounts: exactly one, `default`.
Updates a billing account: changes plan, spend limit, or billing email.

Starts saving a payment method for the org: returns a client secret the
console confirms with Stripe.js, so card data never reaches Sylphx. The
saved method becomes the account's default and is charged off-session
for each finalized invoice.

A seller operator records an externally verified full invoice payment.
The platform-only scope cannot be granted by customer owners/admins.
The invoice name identifies the customer, not the seller. References are
immutable and idempotent per org and method; conflicting reuse is refused.
Lists an org's usage reports, one per billing period.

Queries usage over any time range, bucketed and grouped: the usage
summary the console charts. Reads rollups; never raw events.

services.doc:
BillingService is Sylphx Billing: the meter and plan catalog, each org's
billing account and plan, its invoices, usage, and budget leases. Usage
arrives through each service's spool, never through this API; no request
path calls Billing.
services.name: billing

methods.doc:
Exchanges the caller's workload identity for a short-lived provider
credential under a trust policy (RFC 8693 token exchange). The
credential is narrowed to the request and cached per installation and
permission set; a permission the Connection lacks is PERMISSION_DENIED
with reason `CapabilityMissing`, never an outage.

services.doc:
BrokerService is the credential service: workload identity in, short-lived
scoped provider credential out.
services.name: broker

methods.doc:
Creates a build: one command or one image over a commit or a tree. The
Operation is done when the build reaches a final state. `run` and
`image` are the short forms.

Cancels a queued or running Build; its lease is released and nothing
is published.

Runs one command over an uploaded tree and settles with its exit code,
like the local command. A caller that gets a failure before the command
started (BUILD_FAILURE_SETUP_FAILED, NO_CAPACITY) may build locally.

Builds an image, with an SBOM and signed provenance, from a commit or an
uploaded tree.

Reads a page of a build's log lines, oldest first. With `wait`, an empty
page on a running build waits up to that long for new lines, so a client
follows the log by passing each `next_page_token` back.
Lists build caches in a project.

Mints the settings a build that runs elsewhere (a laptop, a CI runner)
uses to reach the cache: the sccache, Turbo and crates mirror doors and a
short-lived token, as environment variables.

Empties a build cache and keeps the cache. The undo is that the next
build refills it.

services.doc:
BuildService is Sylphx Build: one command or one image over a commit or an
uploaded tree, on an offline build lease beside a warm workspace, with one
cache per project. Images carry an SBOM and signed SLSA provenance, all
written to Sylphx Artifacts by digest.
services.name: build

methods.doc: Lists config flags in an environment.
Creates a config flag; the Operation is done when every cell serves it.

Updates a config flag; the change rolls out in waves and the Operation is
done when every cell serves it.
Deletes a config flag; evaluators then get their compiled-in fallback.

Evaluates config flags of an environment for one evaluation context:
each flag's value, and why. Browsers and mobile apps call it with a
publishable key holding `config:evaluate`, which reads values, never
rules.

The environment's flags and segments in one read, for SDKs that
evaluate locally. Poll it with `if_none_match` set to the last `etag`:
an unchanged ruleset answers `not_modified` and nothing else.
Lists config segments in an environment.
Updates a config segment; every flag naming it follows.
Deletes a config segment; refused while a flag names it.
Lists config changes in an environment.

services.doc:
ConfigService is Sylphx Config: dynamic configuration and feature flags
evaluated in each cell from that cell's snapshot.
services.name: config

methods.doc: Deletes a connection provider; it must have no connections.
Records an installation; the controller confirms it with the provider.
Forgets a connection. The installation itself is removed at the provider.

services.doc:
ConnectionsService is Sylphx Connections: Connection Providers and their
installations as Resources.
services.name: connections

methods.doc:
Writes an object's bytes, replacing the current version. `body` is the
base64 of the bytes.
Reads an object and its bytes (`body`, base64).
Lists a bucket's objects in key order.
Deletes an object's current version (history is kept).

Writes a value. Without `ttl_seconds` the namespace default applies; zero
means no expiry.
Lists a namespace's values in key order.
Adds `delta` (default 1) to an integer value, creating it at zero.

Reads up to 1000 keys at once (MGET). Answers one entry per key, in
order; an absent or expired key keeps its key and has no `value`.
Sets fields of a hash (HSET), creating it.
Reads one field of a hash (HGET); an absent field has no `value`.
Reads every field of a hash (HGETALL).

Reads several fields of a hash (HMGET), one per field, in order; an
absent field has no `value`.
Pushes values onto the head of a list (LPUSH), creating it.
Reads a range of a list (LRANGE); negative indexes count from the end.
Pops values from the head of a list (LPOP); an emptied list is removed.
Reads the length of a list (LLEN); an absent key has length zero.
Adds members to a sorted set or updates their scores (ZADD), creating it.

Reads a range of a sorted set by rank, lowest score first (ZRANGE);
negative indexes count from the end.
Reads a member's score (ZSCORE); an absent member has no `score`.
Reads the size of a sorted set (ZCARD); an absent key has size zero.

Walks a namespace's keys that match a glob (SCAN). Call again with the
returned `cursor` until it is empty.

Sets a key's time to live (EXPIRE) without rewriting its value; zero
makes it persistent.
Writes a document to a search index, replacing the current version.

Changes some fields of a document and keeps the rest: a JSON merge patch
(RFC 7396). The version goes up by one.

Searches an index by text, by vector, or both, best match first, with
filters and paging.

Runs several searches of one index in one request, 1 to 10, and answers
each in request order.
Creates a database. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.
Deletes a database. Fails while `spec.deletion_protection` is set.

Returns how to connect to the database: its endpoint and its own engine
credentials. The credentials are not API keys and are returned only here.

Replaces the database's engine credentials; the old ones stop working once
the new ones are served.

Restores the database in place to a point in time inside its retention
window; the database is unavailable while it restores.
Lists kv namespaces in a environment.

Creates a kv namespace. The Operation is done when the controller settles
it.
Deletes a kv namespace. Fails while `spec.deletion_protection` is set.

Returns how to connect to the KV namespace: its endpoint and its own
engine credentials. The credentials are not API keys and are returned only
here.

Replaces the KV namespace's engine credentials; the old ones stop working
once the new ones are served.
Creates a bucket. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.
Deletes a bucket. Fails while `spec.deletion_protection` is set.

Returns how to connect to the bucket: its endpoint and its own engine
credentials. The credentials are not API keys and are returned only here.

Replaces the bucket's engine credentials; the old ones stop working once
the new ones are served.
Lists search indexs in a environment.

Creates a search index. The Operation is done when the controller settles
it.
Deletes a search index. Fails while `spec.deletion_protection` is set.

Returns how to connect to the search index: its endpoint and its own
engine credentials. The credentials are not API keys and are returned only
here.

Replaces the search index's engine credentials; the old ones stop working
once the new ones are served.

services.doc:
DataPlaneService is the data plane of Sylphx Data: object bytes, key-value
entries (strings, counters, hashes, lists, and sorted sets), and search
documents in an environment's buckets, KV namespaces, and search indexes. It is
served by Data itself at its origin, not by the Resource API, and is called
with the environment's secret key (`SYLPHX_API_KEY`); the key's org,
project, and environment are the tenant. Every call carries a new
`Sylphx-Effect-Id`, which the SDK sends and reuses on retries.

The buckets, namespaces, and indexes themselves are Resources of
DataService. The
messages here are Data's wire format
(`services/data/proto/sylphx/data/v1/data.proto`), field for field; Data
answers ProtoJSON (camelCase names, 64-bit integers and bytes as strings).
services.name: data

methods.doc: Lists an org's entitlements: exactly one, `default`.

services.doc:
EntitlementService is the read-only view of Sylphx Entitlement. Billing
writes it through the Resource store; this service has no mutation.
services.name: entitlement

methods.doc:
Publishes CloudEvents into a Topic, atomically. Replaying the same
`source` + `id` with the same payload returns the stored event; a
different payload fails with RESOURCE_ALREADY_EXISTS.
Enqueues messages directly, without a Subscription.
Leases up to `max_messages` ready messages for the visibility timeout.

Acknowledges leased messages; each is removed. A lease that is stale
(expired or superseded) is reported, not applied.

Returns leased messages to the Queue after `delay`; each nack counts as a
delivery.

Moves dead-lettered messages, optionally bounded by dead-letter time, back
to ready.

Redelivers every dead-lettered delivery to the endpoint created in a time
range, each as a new attempt.

Replaces the endpoint's signing secret and returns the new one, once
(`status.signing_secret`). For 24 hours deliveries carry a signature with
each secret, so a receiver can switch without dropping one.

Sends a test event (`type` `sylphx.webhook.test`) to the endpoint alone,
through the same signing, retries, and delivery log as any other event.
Redelivers one delivery now, as a new attempt.

Publishes one message to the channel: it is appended to the channel's
history and pushed to every connected client. A retry with the same
Idempotency-Key returns the first message.

Mints a subscribe token (`rtt_…`) for this channel alone, at most an hour
long, for a browser or device that holds no key. A token that names a
client id enters the channel's presence while it is connected.
Gets one retained message of a channel.
Lists a channel's retained messages, oldest first.
Gets one client present in a channel.
Lists the clients present in a channel now.

services.doc:
EventsService is Sylphx Events: the event bus, queues, outbound and inbound
webhooks, and realtime channels. Publish, lease, ack, and delivery run in
each cell from that cell's snapshot.
services.name: events

methods.doc: Creates a service. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.
Holds a Rollout at its current wave.
Stops a Rollout; the cells it reached return to the previous Release.
Creates a preview. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.
Lists source links in a project.

Creates a source link. The Operation is done when the controller settles
it.

services.doc:
HostingService is Sylphx Hosting: Services that build from source or run an
existing Artifact, ship as Releases in waves, get a Preview per pull
request, and read their source through a SourceLink.
services.name: hosting

methods.doc: Creates a key; the signer generates its first version.
Updates a key's rotation period, deletion protection, or metadata.
Deletes a key and schedules every version's destruction.

Rotates a key: adds a version and makes it primary. Older versions keep
verifying and decrypting until destroyed.
Signs data or a digest with a SIGN key. Every use is audited.
Verifies a signature made by a SIGN key.
Encrypts data with an ENCRYPT key.
Decrypts a ciphertext made by Encrypt with this key.
Computes a MAC of data with a MAC key.
Verifies a MAC made by a MAC key, in constant time.

Schedules a key version's destruction after a 24-hour grace; the
primary version cannot be destroyed.

services.doc:
KeysService is Sylphx Keys: non-exportable keys on the regional signer.
Callers use a key; no method returns key material.
services.name: keys

methods.doc:
Deletes a space. A space that still holds records is refused with
`INVALID_STATE` unless `force` is set, which deletes its episodes and
facts too.

Updates a knowledge schema. An accepted update publishes a new
revision; a change that would invalidate existing records is refused
with `INVALID_FIELD`.

Deletes a knowledge schema. A schema a space still accepts is refused
with `RESOURCE_IN_USE`.

Lists a space's episodes, newest first. The filter is limited to
`kind` and `extraction`.

Records an episode and returns at once (`remember`); extraction reads
it afterwards.

Deletes an episode, the facts that cite only it, and its search and
embedding entries; facts that also cite other episodes are re-scored.

Lists the entities the caller may see. The filter is limited to
`entity_type` and `lifecycle`.

Creates an entity in a space. An entity whose external id already
names one in the graph is refused with `RESOURCE_ALREADY_EXISTS`, which
names it; use Update with `allow_missing` to upsert.

Updates an entity. With `allow_missing` it is the structured upsert
(`upsert_entity`): an entity matched by `external_ids` is updated,
otherwise one is created.

Deletes an entity and every fact about it. With `force` it is a
data-rights erasure: the episodes the person wrote are deleted too, with
their search and embedding entries.

Merges other entities into this one: their facts and external ids
resolve to it. The merge is recorded and reversible with `:split`; it is
never a silent rewrite.

Splits a merged entity back out of this one, with the facts and
external ids it brought.

Returns one entity's profile in one call (`entity`): the entity, its
current facts in both directions, the entities they name and the recent
episodes about it, trimmed to what the caller may see. A read with a
request body.

Searches the graph (`recall`): hybrid lexical and semantic search over
episodes and facts, fused by reciprocal rank, then at most two hops of
expansion from the top entities. Returns a context pack with citations,
built only from records the caller may see.

Answers a question through Sylphx AI (`ask`), from a context pack built
only from records the caller may see, with citations to its episodes.

Lists a space's facts. The filter is limited to `subject`, `predicate`,
`object` and `provenance.channel`; superseded facts are listed only with
`show_superseded`.

Records a fact in a space (`relate`). A fact that contradicts a current
one with the same subject and a single-valued predicate closes the older
fact; nothing is overwritten.

Deletes a fact. Deletion is for data that must go; a fact that stopped
being true is closed with `:close`.

Closes a fact (`close_fact`): it stopped holding in the world at
`valid_end_time`. The fact stays readable for questions about the time
before the close.

services.doc:
KnowledgeService is Sylphx Knowledge: one permission-aware knowledge graph
that people, apps and agents write while they work and read through search
with citations. Episodes are the sources; entities and relations (facts)
are what is known, each with provenance and valid and recorded time.
Every record lives in one Space, and a caller sees a record only through a
space it may read, so a context pack or an answer never cites a source the
caller cannot open.
services.name: knowledge

methods.doc:
Reads the source files and the committed translations into the catalog,
then translates what is new or stale. Each call is idempotent and works
within a bounded time; call again until `pending` is 0.

Returns the catalog's files per locale in the requested format, with the QA
report. A read with a request body, like a query.

Lists catalog entries. The filter is limited to `state`, `locale`, and
`qa_state`.

Sets the text of one locale as a human override that AI never overwrites.
QA runs on the text first; a text with a QA error is rejected with
`INVALID_FIELD`, and the problem lists the findings.

Removes the human override of one locale; the next sync may translate it
again.

services.doc:
LocalizationService is Sylphx Localization: translate an app's strings in CI
with AI, a translation memory, and a glossary. A Catalog holds the source
messages and their translations; `:sync` translates what is new or changed,
and `:export` returns the files per locale with a QA report. Translation
happens only in these calls, never at build or run time.
services.name: localization

methods.doc: Updates the environment's catalog: its features and products, whole.

Pushes the catalog to the merchant account's processor now: products and
prices by lookup key; an amount change makes a new price.

Gets the environment's checkout policy: which buyer countries consumer
checkout refuses. An environment that never wrote one refuses none.
Updates the environment's checkout policy, whole.
Creates a store connection; its credential is sealed and never returned.
Updates a store connection; a new credential replaces the stored one.
Deletes a store connection and its sealed credential.

Verifies a store purchase with the store, binds it to the subject, and
returns its record and a signed grant. Re-verifying returns the same
record and grant. Called from the app's server with a secret key that
holds `billing:write`; a publishable key cannot call it.

Verifies a store purchase for an app with no server: called with the
environment's publishable key (`billing:client`), the subject is an
install id (`inst_` and a UUID), and Money completes the purchase with the
store (acknowledges or consumes it) so the app never calls the store's
server API. Works only on store connections that set `client_verify`.
Re-calling returns the same record and grant.

Cancels a web subscription, now or at the period end, and optionally
refunds its last payment (for example a statutory cancellation window).
Resumes a web subscription set to cancel at its period end.

Changes the seat quantity of a web subscription, now, and syncs the
processor's subscription item to it. A retry with the same
`Idempotency-Key` (required) and the same request changes nothing twice.

Move a web subscription onto another recurring catalog plan.

Stripe changes the subscription's one item and bills the difference as
`proration_behavior` says; Money reads the subscription back and replaces
its entitlements from it. Needs an `Idempotency-Key` unless `validate_only`.
A store subscription is refused (`store_managed`): the store owns it.
Answers whether a subject holds a feature now, and how much of it.

Creates a manual entitlement grant (support, comp, grace). Append-only;
needs the approval-class scope. The approver recorded is the key's principal.

Starts connecting a Stripe account: returns the processor's authorisation
URL for an org owner to open, which the processor's redirect completes.
With a restricted key in the request the account connects at once
instead, and the connected merchant account comes back in the response.
Reads the connected account back from the processor.
Disconnects the account: Sylphx loses access; checkout is refused.
Updates the merchant account's own settings: the fields named in `update_mask`.
Creates a hosted checkout for a subject.

Lists where the environment's consumer sales stand against each
jurisdiction's digital-services tax registration threshold, per its own
window. EU and UK have no threshold and are not tracked.
Creates a customer portal session for a subject.

Generates a licence key: Money creates the Ed25519 key, seals it, and never
returns the private half. Needs the approval-class scope, which the developer
role does not hold.

Imports an existing Ed25519 key (PKCS8), for a key already pinned in shipped
clients. Refused unless the expected public key is the imported key's public
half.

Retires a licence key: it stops signing new terms and stays exported for
verification.
Gets a licence key (its public half, never the private).

Lists a subject's unexpired offline licence tokens of paid orders, for
support. Re-derived from the frozen terms: the same bytes as at purchase.
Updates the usage settings, the enforcement switch included. A change is recorded with who made it.
Creates or updates a usage tier.

Reserves usage before the work starts. Refused with PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED (spend limit, no payment method) or INVALID_STATE (suspended) only while enforcement is on; while it is dark the reservation is granted and the refusal is recorded.
Settles a reservation with what was used; the unused part returns to headroom. A settle after expiry still records the usage.
Releases a reservation that used nothing.
Records usage directly, only for a meter the merchant marked reservation-optional.

Records a batch of already-incurred usage from the merchant's own servers
(Stripe's meter-event model): the caller is a key of the merchant's own org
holding the exact grant `billing:metering:ingest`, which no wildcard covers,
and each event names its subject with no subject proof. Each event is keyed
by its project, meter, meter version and event id: a replay is a no-op
(`duplicate`), and the same key with different content is a `conflict` and
never counted. One result per event, in request order.
Reads a subject's standing: active, past due or suspended, whether a payment method is on file, headroom and the threshold.

Gives a subject credit. Append-only: a change is a new grant that supersedes the old. Refused with INVALID_STATE (`tax_treatment_unsupported`) for `post_tax_settlement` while the merchant has automatic tax on.
Releases a held invoice for collection, audited with who and why. Grant expiry or replacement never does.
Creates or updates a usage meter. The unit cannot change once it has recorded usage.
Appends a price to a meter's history. It applies from its effective time on and never rewrites usage already rated.
Lists meter prices, newest first; filter by `meter`.

Gets a revenue source, with its freshness. Revenue reporting
(docs/adr/ADR-01M40HRQT0VSXZ1WANP8M318F2) is org-wide: `revenue:read` or
`revenue:write`, held by an org-wide key or an org owner's or admin's
session only; a project or environment key is refused.
Lists the org's revenue sources, with their freshness.

Registers a revenue source. The `money` source is implicit and never
created here.
Renames, pauses or resumes a revenue source, or changes its settings.

Deletes a revenue source and the facts it reported. The `money` source
cannot be deleted; pause it instead.

Syncs a revenue source now, or backfills a period. A `money` source
fills any booked fact its environment's ledger holds and the facts lack;
a paused source, or one whose connector has not shipped yet, is refused
(`INVALID_STATE`).

Gets the org's revenue over a period: totals by day or month, split by
source or product, gross or net, in one reporting currency, with the
basis of each bucket, the sources that report late, and what has no
rate yet. Reads only the daily roll-up, bounded by a 5 second statement
timeout. For example `sylphx money revenue summary --period mtd
--split source`.
Lists the org's revenue facts, newest day first, for audit and export.

Lists the exchange rates Money converts at (units per US dollar by day),
for any reader that converts revenue.

services.doc:
MoneyService is Sylphx Money's customer payments: an app sells to its own
users through the stores and processors Money integrates once, and asks one
question on its request path, "does this subject have this feature"
(docs/services/money/customer-payments.md).
services.name: money

methods.doc: Creates a domain. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.
Checks the verification record now instead of at the next sweep.
Creates a route. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.
Lists egress identitys in a project.

Creates an egress identity. The Operation is done when the controller
settles it.
Lists private links in a environment.

Creates a private link. The Operation is done when the controller settles
it.

services.doc:
NetworkService is Sylphx Network: verified domains, exact routes served by
each cell's edge from its snapshot, certificates Sylphx terminates, declared
egress addresses, and private links.
services.name: network

methods.doc: Checks the domain's DNS records now instead of on the next sweep.
Re-checks the sender's registration or credentials now.
Cancels a Message whose deliveries have not been handed off.
Deletes a mailbox and its inbound email.

Removes an address's personal data from every inbound email of the
mailbox that it sent or that names it, keeping the dedupe keys so a poll
never brings the mail back.
Deletes a mailbox OAuth app; refused while a mailbox uses it.

Mints a mailbox connect link for one end user; the response carries its
`url`, which no later call returns.
Lists a mailbox's inbound email in feed order, oldest first.
Cancels a Broadcast; messages already admitted still deliver.

services.doc:
NotifyService is Sylphx Notify: messages to people over email, SMS, push,
and in-app inbox, with preferences, suppression, templates, and broadcasts.
Notify is built on Sylphx Events as an ordinary customer.
services.name: notify

methods.doc:
Ingests a batch of log entries atomically. The same `Idempotency-Key` and
digest replays the same batch; a different digest under the key conflicts.

Queries the environment's log entries over a bounded interval; follow a
trace with `trace_id = "..."`.

Ingests a batch of spans atomically; a span's parent and time invariants
are validated. Replay rules are those of WriteLogEntries.

Queries the environment's traces over a bounded interval, returning
summaries without spans.
Gets a generation: one Sylphx AI call.

Lists the environment's Sylphx AI calls, newest first, within the trace
retention; filter by `request_model`, `outcome`, `api_key`, `start_time`,
`tags.<key>` and the other filterable fields.

Lists error groups; filter by `state`, `service_name`, and
`last_seen_time`.

Captures one error occurrence. It is grouped by `fingerprint` when the
caller sets one, else by exception type and the symbolicated in-app
stack; release is never part of the group. A new occurrence reopens a
resolved group. Secrets and personal data are scrubbed by the
environment's Scrubbing Policy before storage. A fingerprint-equal replay
bills no second new-error unit. Under quota pressure the response says
what to sample. Browsers call it with a publishable key that holds
`observability:ingest` (CORS allowed, rate-limited per environment).
Resolves an error group; a new occurrence reopens it.
Reopens a resolved or acknowledged error group.

Uploads a source map for one release and minified file. Uploading the
same release and file again replaces it.
Gets a source map (without its content).
Lists source maps, newest first; filter by `release`.

services.doc:
ObservabilityService is Sylphx Observability's log, trace, and error
surface: ingest through the emitter-side buffer, tenant-fenced bounded
queries, and error-group triage. Observability is only ever a soft
dependency.
services.name: observability

methods.doc:
Creates or replaces a namespace's rules. Existing channels follow the new
rules from their next message; shortening history trims at the next
publish.

Deletes a namespace, its channels' history and presence, and closes the
subscriptions on them.

Publishes a message to a channel. The namespace must exist. The server
publishes regardless of `client_publish`. A repeated Sylphx-Effect-Id
publishes once.

Lists a channel's messages after a cursor, oldest first. With
`wait_seconds`, an empty result waits up to that long for the first new
message and answers as soon as one arrives: this is how an agent
subscribes.
Lists who is present on a channel.

Mints a connection or channel token for an end user. The customer's
server calls it with the secret key after authenticating the user, and
hands the token to the client.

Binds a bus Subscription's matching events to a channel: each event the
Subscription matches is published to the channel, with the event's
CloudEvents `type` as the message event and its `data` as the payload. The
Subscription itself is an Events Resource (`sylphx.events.v1`); this call
only names the channel it feeds, and replaces the Subscription's earlier
binding.

services.doc:
ChannelService is the Channel API of Sylphx Realtime: the server side that
configures namespaces, publishes, reads history, lists presence, and mints
the tokens clients connect with. It is served by the Events service at the
Realtime origin, not by the Resource API, and is called with the
environment's secret key (`SYLPHX_API_KEY`); the key's org, project and
environment are the tenant. Clients connect with a token over the Sylphx
channel protocol v1 (`protocol.proto`).

The same calls become MCP tools. An agent cannot hold a socket, so
ListMessages with `wait_seconds` is its subscribe.
services.name: realtime

methods.doc: Lists releases in an environment, newest first by default.
Creates a release: admits it and rolls it out in waves. The Operation is done when the release is live or halted.

services.doc:
ReleaseService is Sylphx Release: the only deployable unit and the progress
of its rollouts. Releases are immutable; there is no Update or Delete.
services.name: release

methods.doc: Lists scale sets in a org.
Creates a scale set. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.
Lists runners in a scale set.

services.doc:
RunnersService is Sylphx Runners: CI runners of a class
`sylphx-<os>-<size>`, one clean Sandboxes lease per job, registered as scale
sets on a Sylphx Runners installation. Runners are read-only: GitHub matches
jobs to runners, and Runners reports them.
services.name: runners

methods.doc: Creates a pool. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.

Lists leases in a environment. Filter on `meta.labels` (for example
`labels.agent = "a_123"`), `status.state`, and `spec.kind`.

Creates a lease: granted now and returned READY (or GRANTED when
`wait_ready` is false), or refused with a typed error. There is no queue.

Extends `expire_time`, never past the shape's longest lease. Does not
change the generation.

Ends a lease with END_REASON_RELEASED; the machine is destroyed and never
leased again, and attached volumes are detached.

Pauses a lease: its disk is kept and its machine destroyed; the
generation increases. Process memory is not kept.

Resumes a paused lease on a machine granted now, or refuses it; the
generation increases.

Replaces a running lease's outbound policy. The generation does not
change; the new policy applies before the call returns.

Mints a lease token for the data plane, bound to the current generation.
Hand it to a process that must not hold the Access key.

Runs one command in the lease to completion and returns its output, capped
at 1 MiB per stream. Long-running or interactive processes use the guest
protocol at `status.endpoints.guest_uri`.

Reads one file from the lease, at most 16 MiB; larger files use the
guest's `/files`.
Writes one file in the lease, at most 16 MiB, creating parent directories.
Lists one directory in the lease.
Removes one file or directory tree in the lease.

Performs computer actions on a DESKTOP, BROWSER, or ANDROID lease, in
order, and returns each action's result and, when `screenshot` is set,
the screenshot taken after the last action. The actions are the Anthropic
computer tool's and OpenAI computer use's, one-to-one
(docs/services/sandboxes/computer-use.md). Refused CONTROL_HELD_BY_HUMAN
while a human holds control.

Opens a read-only live view of a lease's display: a short-lived viewer
token bound to the lease and its generation, an embeddable URL, and the
WebRTC signaling endpoint with ICE servers. Input needs control
(AcquireLeaseControl).

Takes exclusive input control of a lease's display. A HUMAN acquire
preempts an AGENT holder and returns a controller stream; an AGENT acquire
is refused CONTROL_HELD_BY_HUMAN while a human holds control. Control
lapses at `ttl`, which the platform caps at 30 minutes.
Releases control held under `epoch`; its controller tokens stop working.
Gets who holds control of a lease's display.
Installs an Android app (APK) on an ANDROID lease.

Lists a lease's events in order. With `wait`, blocks up to that long
for an event after `page_token` (long poll).
Updates a volume: grows `spec.size_gib` and edits metadata.

Deletes a volume and destroys its data. Refused RESOURCE_IN_USE while it
is attached.
Captures a running lease's disk as a snapshot.

services.doc:
SandboxesService is Sylphx Sandboxes: isolated machines leased for a bounded
time, granted immediately or refused with a typed reason, and destroyed
before anyone else can touch them.
Every agent-computer surface is here: exec and files, computer actions that
map one-to-one onto the Anthropic computer tool and OpenAI computer-use
actions and return the post-action screenshot in the same call, CDP, live
streams, and human takeover. The streaming guest protocol (E2B envd) is
served at `status.endpoints.guest_uri`.
services.name: sandboxes

methods.doc: Creates a secret, without a value; add one with CreateSecretVersion.
Deletes a secret and destroys every version.
Adds a value to a secret as its newest version. The value is never returned.
Disables a secret version: bindings stop delivering it.
Destroys a secret version's value irrecoverably.

Reads a secret version's value back. Break-glass: a separate permission,
audited on every call, and never exposed to MCP.
Lists secret bindings in an environment.
Gets a profile: its kind, grants, sites and latest version; never a value.
Lists the profiles of an environment.

Creates an empty profile; its first version is written by a write-back
mount (`:open` with WRITE_BACK, then `:commit`).

Updates a profile's grants or declared paths. Granting a mount is this
call: nothing else adds a grant.

Deletes a profile; with `force`, a profile that has versions too, which
destroys every version.

Mounts a profile for one session: returns the state of one version and,
for WRITE_BACK, an attachment that `:commit` writes through until it
expires. Every call is audited with the caller's context; the caller's
principal needs a grant of at least the requested mode.

Writes a mounted profile back as a new version, by compare-and-set on the
version the attachment was opened at (or last committed). When another
write landed first, nothing is lost: the result is still a new version,
merged site by site with the newer write winning, and marked as a
conflict.
Gets a profile version: its sites and lineage; never a value.
Lists a profile's versions, newest first.

services.doc:
SecretsService is Sylphx Secrets: write-only, versioned values and the
bindings that deliver them. Reading a value back is the separate break-glass
permission `secrets:access`.
services.name: secrets

methods.doc:
Updates a schedule; with `allow_missing` it creates the schedule when it
does not exist, so its short name `schedule` is an upsert by name.
Pauses a Schedule: no fire starts a Run until it is resumed.
Resumes a paused Schedule; missed fires follow `catchup_window`.

Starts a Run of a Workflow, now or after `start_delay` or at
`schedule_time`. `run_id` is the caller's key: the same key and intent
return the same Run, a changed intent is refused.
An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is
`USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

Starts a batch: a parent Run that fans out one child Run per item, each
with a stable index and count.

Sends a named signal to a running Run; a `wait` op for that name resumes
with its payload. A signal to a closed Run fails with INVALID_STATE.
An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is
`USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

Requests cancellation. Timers and waits stop; a running invocation is not
interrupted: the handler receives one final invocation with `cancel:
true`, and the Run ends `cancelled` when it answers.
An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is
`USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

Waits up to `timeout` (at most 60s) for the Run to close, then returns it,
closed or not. Its short name is `result`: the closed Run carries the
handler's output or error.
An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is
`USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.
Reads a page of the Run's immutable history, projected to Sylphx events.
Updates a job. Runs already started keep the generation they pinned.

Starts a run of a Job now. The same `Idempotency-Key` returns the same
run for 24h; a Schedule fire uses `{job}:{intended time}`. With
concurrency `forbid`, a start while a run is active fails with
INVALID_STATE.
Lists a job's runs, newest first.

Cancels a job run: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 30s. A closed run fails
with INVALID_STATE.

Reads a page of a job run's log lines, oldest first. With `wait`, an
empty page on a running run waits up to that long for new lines, so a
client follows the log by passing each `next_page_token` back.

Updates a distributed job. Runs already started keep the generation they
pinned.

Starts a run of a distributed job. The same `Idempotency-Key` returns the
same run for 24h.
Gets a distributed run: its state, shard and worker counts, and usage.
Lists a distributed job's runs, newest first.

Cancels a distributed run: workers get SIGTERM and 30s, then leases are
released; finished shards are kept. A closed run fails with INVALID_STATE.

Appends shards to a run started with an open manifest; `close` ends the
manifest, and the run ends once those shards are done.
Reads a page of the run's shards, in queue order.
Reads a page of the run's workers.

services.doc:
WorkflowsService is Sylphx Workflows: durable execution, schedules, timers,
and runs. Workflows is the one writer of these types.
services.name: workflows
